description: Misinformation has spread online about who is able to vote in the Alberta referendum. The CBC's fact-check team debunks claims about non-residents voting.
title: Fact check: Can non-residents vote in the Alberta referendum?

author: Diona Macalinga
description: A beluga whale and dolphin that died within weeks of being transferred out of Marineland had been experiencing a list of health complications and organ abnormalities that could've developed prior to the transfer, Oceanogràfic València said in a news release on Oct. 14.
title: Ex-Marineland beluga that died in Spain developed 'complex clinical condition,' aquarium says

author: Natalie Stechyson
description: The family of a man mauled to death by a tiger at a U.K. wildlife park on Saturday is pleading with people to stop sharing footage of the attack online, calling it "deeply offensive" and painful. The statement from the family of 23-year-old William Chapman came after U.S. President Donald Trump shared a clip of the fatal attack on his Truth Social platform Tuesday.
title: What to know about the deadly U.K. tiger attack — and the 'offensive' video shared by Trump

description: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday, ‌after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer.
title: Pope back on his feet, eating normally following cancer diagnosis

author: Padraig Moran
description: Lawyer Thomas Giuffra, who is representing Jane Doe in her civil lawsuit, said the incident is part of escalating threats against the woman, who is identified only as Jane Doe in court documents but has faced concerted efforts to publish her identity online.
title: Jane Doe’s family home hit with swatting attack after Cornell rape allegations: lawyer

author: Ted Anthony
description: Katie Zacharia made her debut as the new White House press secretary on Tuesday, answering only a handful of questions from journalists and failing to impress some observers — including some who had held the job before her.
title: Katie Zacharia fails to impress in brief debut as White House press secretary

author: Alexandra Mae Jones
description: If you're tired of dressing up as salt-and-pepper shakers, for a couple hundred bucks, you and a partner can snag Angine de Poitrine couple's costume from Party Expert, one of Canada's biggest party supply stores.
title: Want to go as Angine de Poitrine for Halloween? You're in luck

description: Andrew Chang breaks down audio of 911 dispatch calls following the failed execution of Christa Pike, revealing how confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials delayed emergency care. Images provided by The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images
title: Botched 911 call: How the failed Christa Pike execution got worse | About That

author: Griffin Jaeger
description: Kelly Clarkson's feud with a Brooklyn shop over a singing mechanical bird just got a lot more expensive —15 million dollars more, to be precise.

title: Kenya confirms 2nd case of Ebola in relative of patient who died earlier this month

description: Delta police say another victim has died as a result of the vehicle crash at Tsawwassen Mills mall on Sept. 30.
title: Injured victim dies following crash at B.C. mall on Truth and Reconciliation Day: police

author: Emily Chung
description: An Italian photographer's "heartbreakingly poignant" photo of a mother elephant carrying her dead calf has won this year's top Wildlife Photographer of the Year award. See a selection of the other winning photos here.
title: Image of mournful elephant mom wins 2026 Wildlife Photographer of the Year

author: Christine Pagulayan
description: More than six decades after leaving Canada, legendary singer-songwriter Joni Mitchell has officially become a U.S. citizen. The announcement has drawn mixed reactions given her outspoken political views.

author: Griffin Jaeger
description: Julia Stiles joining Dancing with the Stars came with one very obvious question: Would she bring Save The Last Dance to the ballroom ? The answer is yes.

description: A third member of the Canadian Armed Forces, and four other people, were arrested and charged in a kidnapping probe that led to the arrest of two other members of Canada’s military reserves, Toronto police announced Wednesday.
title: 3rd member of Canadian Armed Forces charged in kidnapping probe: Toronto police

author: The Associated Press
description: U.S. President Donald Trump said an oil, gas and mineral exploration is set to begin in Greenland. It wasn't immediately clear what exploration or developments he was referring to.
title: Trump says oil, gas and mineral exploration in Greenland is set to begin. It's not that simple

description: German authorities opened an investigation into possible sexual harassment after a robot controlled by two young men touched the buttocks of a 16-year-old girl and made thrusting movements toward her, police said.
title: Robot controlled by 2 men gropes teen girl in Germany. Police call it 'new territory'

author: Katie DeRosa
description: Lorne Doerkson didn't set out to lead the B.C. Conservatives. He was selected as the safe choice after the resignation of Kerry-Lynne Findlay. While most British Columbians didn't know much about the 58-year-old, he's now leading a party that polls suggest is ahead of David Eby's NDP.
title: Unexpected leader: Lorne Doerkson pitches himself to British Columbians

author: Taryn Grant
description: Months after the death of their baby girl, Carly Wedge and Alexandre Genest are touring around Nova Scotia on their bicycles — working through their grief, raising money for the hospital that tried to save her, and spreading the word about a vaccine that’s in development.
title: N.S. couple cycles through their grief as hospital tests vaccine to save other babies

description: Separatism is on the minds of many Canadians right now, but these ideas aren't exactly new. And Nova Scotia once led the charge. The CBC's Richard Cuthbertson explains the history — and what we can learn from it.
title: What can we learn from Nova Scotia's own separatist movement?

description: An administrative building belonging to Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company Saudi Aramco in the eastern city of Dhahran was attacked, causing a limited fire, the Energy Ministry said in a statement Wednesday, as fighting between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and the kingdom intensified.
title: Saudi Aramco administrative building attacked by Houthis, limited fire reported

author: Abby Hughes
description: The cyberattack on French supermarkets earlier this week that left hundreds of fridges worth of food spoiled should be a wake-up call about the vulnerabilities of digitized systems and devices that are connected to the internet, cybersecurity experts say.
title: A fridge hack spoiled food in hundreds of French supermarkets. Cybersecurity experts say it's a wake-up call

author: Natalie Stechyson
description: A winery in Tuscany is reeling after thieves made off with about 30,000 bottles of some of Italy's most prized wines last week in what the producer described as the country’s largest wine theft on record.

description: A U.S. judge is expected to hand down a sentence Wednesday for Luciano Frattolin, a Montreal man who was found guilty in August of the second-degree murder of his nine-year-old daughter, Melina.
title: Montreal man convicted of killing 9-year-old daughter to be sentenced today

author: Mark Gollom
description: When Ukrainian drones hit three data centres owned by Russian technology and AI company Yandex this weekend, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy initially said it resulted in a sudden drop in pro-Russia bot activity on social media. Some experts are casting doubt on his claim, instead suggesting people are misinterpreting data collected after the strikes.
title: Why Zelenskyy's claims that Ukraine drone attack halted Russian bot traffic don't hold up
